primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Wilson disease due to biallelic ATP7B pathogenic variants
mechanism: ATP7B is a P-type copper-transporting ATPase in hepatocytes that incorporates copper into ceruloplasmin and transports excess copper into bile. Loss of ATP7B function impairs biliary copper excretion, causing hepatic and extrahepatic copper accumulation.
vignette: A young adult develops chronic liver disease, a tremor, dysarthria, and Kayser-Fleischer rings. Serum ceruloplasmin is low and urinary copper excretion is increased. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in ATP7B.
lead: The normal protein affected in this patient performs which of the following functions?
correct: Transports copper within hepatocytes for incorporation into ceruloplasmin and excretion into bile
distractors: Transports copper from intestinal enterocytes into the portal circulation
Exports iron from enterocytes and macrophages through ferroportin
Transfers triglycerides onto apoB during hepatic VLDL assembly
Conjugates bilirubin with glucuronic acid in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum
distractor_notes: ATP7A is the copper transporter central to intestinal copper absorption and systemic distribution; ATP7B is the hepatocyte copper transporter impaired in Wilson disease.
Ferroportin mediates cellular iron export, not hepatic copper handling.
Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein is involved in apoB-lipoprotein assembly, not copper transport.
UGT1A1 catalyzes bilirubin glucuronidation and is unrelated to ATP7B-mediated copper transport.
key_expl: ATP7B is a hepatocyte P-type copper-transporting ATPase. It moves copper for incorporation into ceruloplasmin and, when copper is abundant, facilitates copper excretion into bile. Loss of ATP7B function therefore causes hepatic copper retention and eventual extrahepatic deposition.
objective: Identify ATP7B as the hepatocyte copper transporter required for ceruloplasmin incorporation and biliary copper excretion in Wilson disease.
